content.value_statement: Frontend teams often produce inconsistent architecture, loading behavior, and performance practices. This skill applies opinionated React and TypeScript standards with checklists and examples.
actual_capabilities: Assesses proposed frontend work with a five-dimension feasibility and complexity index.
Defines feature-based folders, import aliases, naming rules, and public export patterns.
Guides typed React component structure, responsibilities, lazy loading, and Suspense boundaries.
Specifies query keys, typed API layers, cache-first reads, mutations, invalidation, and error handling.
Covers TanStack Router routes, lazy components, parameters, navigation, layouts, and breadcrumb loaders.
Provides MUI v7 styling, strict TypeScript, memoization, debouncing, and effect cleanup guidance.
limitations: Targets React, TypeScript, TanStack Query, TanStack Router, and MUI v7 rather than every frontend stack.
Provides guidance and examples but does not install dependencies, run builds, or execute tests.
Uses project-specific helpers such as SuspenseLoader, apiClient, and useMuiSnackbar that require local equivalents.
Cannot confirm accessibility, runtime performance, or integration behavior without reviewing and testing the target repository.

use_cases.title: Create a React Feature
use_cases.description: Create a React feature with consistent folders, typed APIs, Suspense boundaries, routes, and MUI styling.

use_cases.title: Standardize Code Reviews
use_cases.description: Review pull requests against a shared checklist for architecture, typing, loading states, styling, and performance.

use_cases.title: Modernize Legacy Screens
use_cases.description: Refactor legacy loading, data fetching, and component organization toward a Suspense-first, feature-based design.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Typed Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a typed React component for [purpose]. Follow the component structure, loading, styling, and feedback rules in these guidelines.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Feature Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a feature named [name] using feature-based folders, a typed API layer, Suspense queries, lazy loading, and public exports.

prompt_templates.title: Review Frontend Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [files] against the frontend guidelines. List architecture, TypeScript, loading, styling, and performance violations, then propose prioritized fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Complex Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor [workflow] for TanStack Router, Suspense-first data fetching, cache-aware mutations, MUI v7, and strict TypeScript. Preserve behavior and identify migration risks.

output_examples.input: Review a React page that fetches user data inside the component and returns an early spinner.
output: The review flags inline data access, the early loading return, missing feature boundaries, and untyped responses.
It recommends a typed feature API, Suspense query, feature-level boundary, and focused component responsibilities.

output_examples.input: Plan a new reporting feature with charts, routes, and export actions.
output_examples.output: The plan defines feature folders, typed API contracts, lazy chart loading, route metadata, query keys, mutation feedback, and performance checks.

output_examples.input: Assess a proposed dashboard before implementation.
output_examples.output: An FFCI assessment rates architectural fit, complexity, performance risk, reusability, and maintenance cost, then recommends proceeding, splitting, or redesigning.

best_practices: Share the target repository structure, framework versions, and existing helper APIs before requesting implementation.
Ask for focused changes and require tests, type checks, and build validation in the target project.
Treat the rules as project defaults and document any justified exceptions during review.
anti_patterns: Applying MUI, TanStack, or Suspense conventions to projects that use different frameworks without adaptation.
Requesting broad rewrites without providing current architecture, dependencies, or acceptance criteria.
Accepting generated examples without checking accessibility, browser behavior, tests, and project-specific contracts.

faq.question: Does this skill write frontend code?
faq.answer: It guides creation and review of React and TypeScript code when an agent can access the target project.

faq.question: Which technology stack does it target?
faq.answer: It targets React, TypeScript, TanStack Query, TanStack Router, MUI v7, and feature-based application architecture.

faq.question: Does it execute scripts or commands?
faq.answer: No. Its files are documentation, although a coding agent may use project tools separately when implementing a request.

faq.question: Can it replace project testing?
faq.answer: No. Generated changes still require type checks, tests, builds, accessibility review, and browser validation.

faq.question: How does it handle data loading?
faq.answer: It favors typed feature API layers, TanStack Query Suspense hooks, cache-first access, and feature-level Suspense boundaries.

faq.question: Can teams adapt the rules?
faq.answer: Yes. Treat them as opinionated defaults and document changes needed for local architecture, libraries, or product requirements.
